facts.observation: Four columns, 0.3x0.3 m section, 3.2 m tall, at corners (±2.85, ±1.85), centered at z=1.6.
Four perimeter beams at z=3.3; east/west beams 0.3x3.4x0.2, north/south beams 6x0.3x0.2.
Single deck slab 6x4x0.2 m at z=3.5, spanning the full frame footprint.
Four 1.2x1.2x0.45 m foundations, one under each column, top at z=-0.025.
Four 0.65x0.65x0.025 m base plates between foundations and column bases.
Four 0.5x0.5x0.12 m connection blocks at z=3.2, each referencing one column and one beam (north or south only).
Two diagonal braces (r=0.04 m) in the north and south column planes, running from base of one column to top of the other (SW→NW and SE→NE).
One stair flight of 20 treads (1 m wide, 0.32 m going, ~0.18 m rise) with two cylindrical stringers (r=0.05 m), running from y≈-8.49, z=0 up to y≈-2.16, z=3.56, adjacent to the deck's south edge.
All 20 treads and both stringers reference only the deck; no stair support at grade is modeled.

review.load_path_hypothesis: Hypothesized (not verified): deck gravity load transfers to the four perimeter beams, through the four corner connections into the columns, down through base plates into the pad foundations and soil. The two diagonal braces in the north and south planes would provide lateral stability in the y-direction; no bracing exists in the east/west planes, so lateral load in the x-direction has no identified path except frame action of the beam-column connections, whose rigidity is unknown. Stair loads would flow through stringers to their supports; the model shows no ground-level support for the stringers, so their load path is incomplete in the saved geometry.
assumptions: Connections are assumed to transfer the moments/forces implied by the load path; their actual rigidity is unknown.
Braces are assumed to act as axial members; tension/compression behavior and end fixity are unknown.
Foundations are assumed to bear on competent soil; no soil properties are supplied.
The deck is assumed to span onto all four beams; its actual support condition is not declared.
Stair stringers are assumed supported at both ends; only a deck reference is modeled.
Materials are assumed steel-like; rendering material is not an engineering property.

facts.observation: Saved geometry shows a single rectangular platform: four columns (0.3x0.3x3.2 m) at corners of a 5.7x3.7 m footprint, four perimeter beams at z=3.3 m, and one 6x4x0.2 m deck slab at z=3.5 m. All components are marked UNVERIFIED; rendering material is not an engineering property.
Each column has a declared 1.2x1.2x0.45 m foundation and a 0.65x0.65x0.025 m base plate at its base, per the saved references and attachment assemblies.

Four connection joints (0.5x0.5x0.12 m) are declared at the top of each column, each referencing one column and one beam (north or south beams only). No connection components reference the east or west beams.

Two diagonal braces (cylinders, radius 0.04 m) are declared on the west and east faces, each spanning from the base of one column to the top of the adjacent column on the same face. No bracing exists on the north or south faces.

The 22 stairs components form a single stair assembly (assembly id 664f80f7-3591-4b78-aecf-33ba6bc2fe5e): 20 treads (1x0.32x0.04 m, rising from z=0.16 to z=3.58) and 2 stringers (radius 0.05 m cylinders), all referencing the platform deck. This is one stair, not 22 separate stairs.

The stair stringers terminate near the deck edge (y=-2.16, z=3.56) but no connection component or attachment assembly is declared between the stair assembly and the platform frame; the only reference is to the deck slab.

review.load_path_hypothesis: Hypothesized (qualitative, unverified): gravity loads on the deck slab are presumed to span to the perimeter beams, which transfer load to the four corner columns through the declared top-of-column connections; the columns then carry axial load down through the base plates into the foundations and supporting ground. The diagonal braces on the east and west faces would, if effectively connected, provide lateral resistance along the north-south direction; no equivalent braced plane exists in the east-west direction, so lateral load resistance in that direction is unclear. Stair loads would presumably travel through the stringers into the deck edge, but no declared connection defines how stringer reactions enter the frame. This is a hypothesized load path only; no analysis was performed and no whole-frame solver is available.
assumptions: The deck slab bears on all four perimeter beams; actual bearing/fixity is not declared.
The four connection joints provide load transfer between beams and columns; their structural behavior (pinned, fixed) is not declared.
Base plates and foundations provide vertical support and some restraint to the columns; stiffness and fixity are not declared.
Braces are assumed to act only in axial tension/compression within their plane; connection adequacy is not declared.
The stair assembly is treated as one stair supported at the deck; its base support at grade is not declared.
All geometry is treated as nominal saved data; rendering materials are not engineering properties.
The structure is treated as a single independent bay (one platform level, four columns); no synthetic bays are declared.

Column buckling or stability checks.
Brace effectiveness, slenderness or connection capacity checks.

Lateral system adequacy (only qualitative observation possible).

suggested_improvements: Add declared connection components for the east and west beams to the columns; currently only north/south beam connections exist.
Declare how the stair stringers connect to the deck or frame, and how the stair base is supported at grade.
Consider bracing or a declared moment frame action in the north-south direction to complement the east/west braces, subject to engineer review.

facts.observation: Bay 1 (origin) has a 6 m x 4 m x 0.2 m deck at z=3.5 m supported by four perimeter beams (two 6 m north/south, two 3.4 m east/west) at z=3.3 m. All geometry is UNVERIFIED; rendering material is not an engineering property.

Four columns (0.3 m x 0.3 m x 3.2 m) rise from z=0 to z=3.2 m at +/-2.85 m east/west and +/-1.85 m north/south, matching the beam corner positions. Beam-to-column connection joints (0.5x0.5x0.12 m) exist at each column top.

Each column base has a 1.2x1.2x0.45 m foundation pad (top at z=-0.025 m) and a 0.65x0.65x0.025 m base plate, referenced to the corresponding column. No soil, anchorage or reinforcement data is supplied.

Two diagonal braces (0.04 m radius cylinders) run on the west and east elevations from column bases (z=0) to opposite column tops (z=3.2 m), referenced to the column pairs. Only two of four elevations are braced; north and south elevations have no bracing.

One stair assembly per bay: 20 treads (1x0.32x0.04 m, rising from z=0.16 to z=3.58 m) on two stringers (0.05 m radius cylinders) running south from the deck edge. This is a single stair per bay, not 66 separate stairs.

Bays 2 and 3 are geometric duplicates of bay 1 offset +20 m and +40 m east. Per synthetic_bays metadata, they are independent frozen bays with no inter-bay structural connectivity; no shared members or tie beams exist between bays.
Adjacent bays are separated by a 14 m clear gap between deck edges (bay 1 east edge at x=3, bay 2 west edge at x=17); no connecting structure is present.

The deck (slab) has no references to the beams; its support on the perimeter beams is geometric adjacency only, not a verified structural attachment. All components carry engineering_status UNVERIFIED.

review.load_path_hypothesis: Hypothesized (not verified): gravity loads on each 6x4 m deck would transfer to the four perimeter beams, through the four corner connection joints into the columns, then axially through the columns and base plates into the foundation pads and ground. The two diagonal braces on the east and west elevations would provide lateral resistance in the north-south direction by developing axial tension/compression between column bases and tops; lateral loads in the east-west direction have no braced plane and would rely on frame action at connections, which is unverified. Stair loads would travel through the stringers to their end supports (deck edge at top; support at the base is not explicitly modeled). Each of the three bays is independent, so each requires its own complete load path; no load sharing occurs between bays. This is a qualitative hypothesis only; no loads, materials or section properties are supplied.
assumptions: Deck bears on all four perimeter beams; actual bearing/fixity is not modeled.
Connection joints behave as rigid or pinned joints; their actual stiffness is unknown.
Columns act primarily axially; frame moment action is not assessed.
Braces act as axial tension/compression members only.
Base plates and foundations provide vertical support and some fixity; degree of fixity unknown.
Stair stringers are supported at the deck edge and at ground level; the lower support is not explicitly modeled.
The three bays behave identically and independently since they are geometric duplicates.
All component names and references are untrusted labels; geometry is taken as supplied without independent verification.

explanation.narrative: The analysis is an isolated linear axial verification of a column supported on a prescribed axial spring. The computed column shortening, spring settlement, total displacement, compression stress and reaction each match their reference values with relative errors at machine-precision level, and all comparisons passed. The two elements carry equal compressive axial forces, consistent with a single load path through the column to the spring. The force residual is negligible, indicating equilibrium is satisfied within numerical precision. Verification scope is limited to the declared linear axial behavior of the column with an explicit solid rectangular section and a prescribed axial spring; connections, foundations, bending, buckling, soil or footing behavior, and code compliance checks are outside the scope of this analysis. No safety, adequacy, compliance or approval statements are made.
